question: Mummy brown owed much of its darkness to bitumen in the bodies. Which Egyptian mummies contain the most?
answer: Late and Graeco-Roman burials. Chemical analysis of mummies found petroleum bitumen absent or rare in early ones, appearing in the New Kingdom and commonest in the Ptolemaic and Roman periods, when far more people were embalmed. Those plentiful late bodies were what dealers could buy. The brown on a Victorian palette came from ordinary townspeople, not pharaohs.
